result.title: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems
result.summary: Improving an agent through successive revisions requires balancing exploration and evaluation under a limited budget. A narrow search can miss useful sequences of edits, while fully evaluating every intermediate version can exhaust the budget before those sequences yield a verified improvement. We introduce Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement (SpecRSI), which drafts executable successor agents before their predecessors are fully evaluated, while requiring complete verification before adoption. Verification-Aware Tree Search (VATS) allocates the budget between further edits and outstanding checks using the predicted verified return of a continuation. Group Verification Optimization (GVO) learns the improver from completed searches while keeping the real evaluator fixed. In the main scientific comparison, terminal gains exceed Janus by 33.3%--40.0%. Additional evaluations show that SpecRSI outperforms Janus in all 50 scientific backbone--task pairs and exceeds MetaRSI-v1 by 1.85%--2.38% in macro-average system score across twenty backbones. Coding-validation success reaches 69.4% versus HGM's 64.3% at a 20.8% lower target-cost index.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement（SpecRSI）：在有限预算下先推测式草拟可执行的继任 agent 再做完整验证，并用验证感知树搜索（VATS）在继续编辑与待完成检验之间分配预算、用组验证优化（GVO）训练改进器，在科学任务与编码验证对比中超过 Janus、MetaRSI-v1 与 HGM。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉/多模态推理无直接关联，但其「按预测的已验证回报分配计算」「先草拟后验证」的做法，可能为 LVR 中的动态计算分配、证据获取与停止决策提供可核查的方法线索。
